VERIFIED 2026-08-01, WRITE_GUIDE_SHAPES lines 15-31: the file-single shape it publishes is {type, path, summary, aliases} — there is NO symbols field, and file-single is the DEFAULT (~97% of notes). Only file-hub carries symbols, via facets. Consequence measured the same day: 2 of 44 notes in this notebook declare ANY anchor symbol, so the anchor channel (paths AND symbols, weight x2) holds paths only, and an agent's code-shaped kb search term has nothing to match. This is a GUIDE gap, not a schema gap — write.ts:39 accepts anchors[{path,symbols}] on a file spec and write.ts:273-278 unions them into the note. Adding symbols to this shape is the cheap half of that fix.

summary: Single source for the kb write spec guide and every write-time WARN, shared by the CLI (kb write, no spec -> guide) and MCP kb_write (parity: identical semantics, only the howto tail differs). flowEvidenceCount scans tmpdir capture markers from ALL THREE hosts (coldstart-kb-/coldstart-cursor-kb-/coldstart-codex-kb- prefixes) for the session's content-read set. 2026-08-01: WRITE_GUIDE_SHAPES now publishes anchors[{path,symbols}] on file-single — it did not before, which is why 2 of 44 notes declared any anchor symbol and code-shaped kb search queries had nothing to match. New missingFieldsWarning(spec,id) reports the fields a note needs to be FINDABLE (aliases for every type but lesson, scope.terms for lesson, anchors[].symbols for file notes) and returns a ready-to-paste re-put carrying the id, so completing a note is one more write and never a lost one; it is a report, not a rejection, because the capture prompt chains writes with && and a non-zero exit would silence every note behind the offending one. flowStepsWarning now takes anchorsAfter (the folded note's anchor count) — judging the SPEC alone made it fire 'this note has NO anchors' at an alias-only update of a flow holding three.

summary: Single source for the kb write spec guide and every write-time WARN, shared by the CLI (kb write, no spec -> guide) and MCP kb_write (parity: identical semantics, only the howto tail differs). flowEvidenceCount scans tmpdir capture markers from ALL THREE hosts (coldstart-kb-/coldstart-cursor-kb-/coldstart-codex-kb- prefixes) for the session's content-read set. This file NO LONGER OWNS THE SHAPES: WRITE_GUIDE_SHAPES is shapesBlock() from hooks/note-shape.mjs and missingFieldsWarning is a loop over checksForSpec(type), so what warns here and what kb repair detects on disk cannot disagree. THE RULE EVERY WARN HERE MUST FOLLOW, learned twice: judge the FOLDED note, never the record just sent. `op: put` appends a record and the note is the fold of the whole log (aliases/anchors union, summary/steps LWW), so a partial update legitimately omits fields it is not changing. flowStepsWarning was fixed for this first — it takes the folded note and delegates to stepsMissingAfterWrite. missingFieldsWarning had the identical defect four lines down and was fixed 2026-08-01: it now takes an optional `after` and a field counts as missing only when missingInSpec(spec) AND missingInNote(after). The AND matters — swapping outright to missingInNote would make the repair-only checks (flow-no-steps, flow-steps-unanchored, both missingInSpec:()=>false) start firing at write time and duplicate flowStepsWarning. With no `after` it falls back to the spec, which is exact for a create.
